chunks: O believers, eat what is good of the food We have given you, and be grateful to God, if indeed you are obedient to Him.

key_terms.طَيِّبَاتِ: Good, pure, and lawful provisions or food

ai.seo_question: What is the connection between eating lawful food and worshipping God in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to establish the permissibility of all good things unless explicitly prohibited, emphasizing that gratitude (shukr) is not merely verbal but manifested through mindful consumption of divine blessings. It underscores the principle that physical sustenance is a means to spiritual elevation, linking the material act of eating directly to the worship of Allah. This perspective highlights the holistic nature of Shia jurisprudence, where daily acts like eating are elevated to acts of devotion when performed with awareness and thankfulness.
